Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Overt ABS markers: particles ye/ti for NPs, Class I pronouns (ako, ka, ya, hila) for persons (Chart 1, p.1; Chart 2, p.3).
curated_comment: Ayta Abenlen (aben1249, ISO abp, Austronesian/Sambalic, Philippines) is a Philippine-type ergative language per Nitsch (2009). GB409_23=1 (nin = ERG/GEN, explicit in Chart 1 and throughout). GB409_24=1: instrumental is expressed with the ERG/GEN particle nin (§3.2.4, p.23). GB409_15 and GB409_19 remain '?' Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: ERG alignment in progressive/imperfective aspect (aN- prefix); agent takes Class II (ERG).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: ERG alignment in perfective aspect (-in- infix); agent takes Class II (ERG).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Past events (na- prefix) maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Non-past/future (m- prefix) clauses maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: Indicative declaratives consistently show ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Imperatives and other non-indicative forms maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Completed/realis clauses maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Irrealis (future, imperative, purpose) maintains ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Agentive A (volitional actors) takes Class II (ERG) pronouns or ERG particle nin.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Source does not discuss non-agentive/experiencer A; insufficient data to determine.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: In Philippine-type system, topical argument is always in ABS; A is always non-topical and ERG. GB409_16=0 is the canonical pattern.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: Non-topical A takes nin/Class II (ERG) consistently in all transitive examples.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: All animate A in examples take ERG case.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No examples of inanimate A in this source; insufficient data.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Main clauses consistently show ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Subordinate clauses maintain ERG alignment (p.6, 19).

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Personal demonstrative pronouns never take ERG because their inherent definiteness requires them to be the absolutive argument (§1.3.1, p.6). Definiteness-based conditioning of ERG.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Chart 1 (p.1) labels nin as 'ERG/GEN'; Class II pronouns used for both agent (ERG) and possessive (GEN) functions (pp.9-10).

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Instrumental adverbs are case-marked with nin (the ERG/GEN marker): antoyhoken lan etak 'they are stabbing with machete' where etak (machete) = instrument marked with nin (§3.2.4, p.23).
